value: This article defines a lattice as an abstract mathematical structure fundamental to order theory and abstract algebra. It can be characterized as a partially ordered set where every pair of elements has a unique least upper bound (join) and greatest lower bound (meet), or equivalently, as an algebraic structure with two binary operations satisfying specific commutative, associative, and absorption laws. The equivalence of these definitions allows lattice theory to integrate both order-theoretic and algebraic perspectives. The text explores various types of lattices, including bounded, complete, distributive, and modular lattices, detailing their properties, morphisms, and substructures, alongside illustrating these concepts with examples and highlighting their diverse applications in fields such as computer science and logic.
